segments.text: The title of the paper shows the motivation of this research is to develop socially behaved artificial agents.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We believe that sociality will become an important point to apply AI in our daily life.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The difficulty to realize social agents is that an appropriate social behavior depends on a given situation or culture.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As described in the bottom figure, we have sociality even in just walking case.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: For example, how fast should we walk or how much distance from others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So if we implement sociality with rule-based program, we have to design a lot of magic number for each situation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is impossible because there are a wide variety of situations.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Due to this, unified mechanism or principle for social behavior is required.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is the challenge.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We assume that we humans have such unified behavior model because we humans can behave socially in diverse situations.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And we develop social engines inspired by human behavior models, namely, free energy principle and active influence.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In this research, we use the active influence for the basis of the behavior model of human life agent.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As you know, active inference is a concept proposed in the free energy principle.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And free energy principle is a unified hypothesis for our cognitive activities.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In the FAP, our cognitive activities are explained by such.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But we have internal models for predicting future of surrounding environment.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Second, we always try to minimize the free energy of the model.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Free energy is defined by this equation, and it intuitively represents uncertainty of prediction.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The interesting point of the FEP is that the internal model inferred not only the hidden state, but also actions for the agent.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That is, the action to be taken is the action which minimizes the free energy of the agent.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is the basic idea of active inference, as I understand it.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Intentional actions also can be explained in the active inference.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In this case, we consider expected free energy, which is the free energy for the future state
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: When considering multi-time step ahead, expected energy at multi-time step ahead is considered as described in the right figure.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Based on the expected free energy for each action, the distribution of the action is determined such that the smaller the expected free energy, the higher the probability of selection.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: When we consider intentional behavior, intentions are considered as requirements of future observations, and rewards according to the future observation are encoded into the last equation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: These are my understanding of the standard active inference and the behavior model of the human life agent based on it.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We extend this active inference to generate the social behavior.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The idea of the extension is explained using a situation in which there are two agents called I and other.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The agent called I is the subject of the action in this explanation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The biological agent under the X3 inference makes predictions about the environment.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: and takes some action to minimize the uncertainty of the prediction.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In this figure, I predict future behavior of the other because the other is an environment, or I. Namely, I act to reduce uncertainty for the other.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So far, this is a standard active inference.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Here, if we consider that the other is also a biological agent, we can assume that the other also acts under the active inference.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Under this idea, we can assume that the other also predicts the future behavior of me, and the other tries to reduce the uncertainty of the prediction about me in this situation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In this understanding, we notice that our action can reduce not only our own free energy, but also that of the others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is because my action affects not only my own free energy, but also the free energy of the others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: If I can predict other's prediction for me, I can act to reduce the free energy of the other.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is the idea of the proposed extension of the active inference.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We extend FEP and active inference from an individual idea to a collective idea.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As described in this image of concept,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The agent marginally shares the brain, and they try to minimize the free energy of the shared brain.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: To release the free energy for the shared brain, we act not only for me, but also for the others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Because of this action for others,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We expect that this idea can be used to generate social behavior, which is a behavior for us, not only for me or only for you.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: To realize this idea, it is necessary to predict other's prediction about myself.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is implemented based on the mirror system and simulation theory.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Hypothesis for the mechanism of empathy.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In the mirror system and simulation theory, it is said that we understand others by simulating others by own bodies.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We consider the idea of using our own body to simulate others as using our internal model to infer other predictions.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The overview of the mechanism is described in the figure.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The agent has the internal model to predict future observations for his own observations.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Moreover, we use the same internal model to predict others' predictions about myself.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Although the model is the same, the input to the model is changed to the observations of the others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: For this,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: the process of inference of other observations is included.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: For example, when the observation is an image, novel view synthesis, which is the problem of generating images from different viewpoints, can be used.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In the other case, as we will discuss in the following evaluation,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In this evaluation, the weight of the
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: On the other hand, the force from the others is larger than the force to the goal.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The agents take behavior in altruistic.
